title: Seller Performance Standing — Clean-Span Relief Points Worksheet
content:
**The quantity.** The active points are the points of every violation recorded on the standing record, less every point reversed and every point already expired or relieved on that record. The clean-span relief is the active points multiplied by the clean-span relief rate of 0.2 and rounded down to a whole point, and it never exceeds the clean-span relief cap of 4 points. The product is worked to four decimal places before it is rounded down.

This worksheet sets out how many violation points a Seller Performance Standing clean-span relief takes off.

## Line by line

| Line | Entry | Source on the seller's standing record |
|---|---|---|
| A | Points of every violation recorded | each recorded policy violation's points |
| B | Points reversed | every reversal entry on the record |
| C | Points already expired or relieved | every points-expiry entry on the record, relief entries included |
| D | Active points | A less B less C |
| E | Rate | 0.2 |
| F | Product | D multiplied by E, to four decimal places |
| G | Rounded down | F rounded down to a whole point |
| H | Clean-span relief | G, or 4 if G is higher than 4 |

## Worked figures (hypothetical record)

A record shows violations recorded for 2, 4 and 8 points (line A: 14), one reversal of 2 points (line B: 2) and points-expiry entries of 3 points (line C: 3). The active points are 14 less 2 less 3, which is 9. Multiplied by 0.2 they give 1.8000; rounded down, 1 point. That is within 4, so the clean-span relief is 1 point.

A second hypothetical record carries 23 active points. Multiplied by 0.2 they give 4.6000, rounded down to 4; the relief is 4 points. With 25 active points the product is 5.0000, rounded down to 5, and the relief is held at 4 points.

## Points of reading

- Rounding is downward only and happens once, after the product is worked to four decimal places: 0.2 multiplied by 4 active points is 0.8000, which rounds down to 0.
- Points already relieved are taken out of the active points in the same way as points that expired, since both stand on the record as points-expiry entries.
